verdict.rationale: cubic's memory-and-learning docs say developers can reply to a review comment explaining what cubic should do differently and it "remembers for next time." Thumbs up/down reactions also calibrate useful versus noisy feedback, so the push-back-and-learn loop is a documented first-party capability. missing for 10: explicit documentation that rejected feedback stops recurring in later reviews (scope, persistence, how learned memories are viewed or managed), independent or hands-on corroboration that the learning actually suppresses repeated comments.

support.subject: As a developer, I can push back on a bad review comment and the reviewer learns — it stops repeating the same rejected feedback

citations.quote: Reply to its comments: Type a response explaining what cubic should do differently, and it remembers for next time
React to suggestions: Thumbs up/down help cubic calibrate what's useful vs noise for your specific codebase
cubic learns your team's unwritten rules from two sources: direct feedback on its comments, and patterns extracted from your senior engineers' historical code reviews.
